<pr_description>
Consider the following PR description:
Ordering problem in admin.RelatedFieldListFilter and admin.RelatedOnlyFieldListFilter
Description
	
RelatedFieldListFilter doesn't fall back to the ordering defined in Model._meta.ordering. 
Ordering gets set to an empty tuple in ​https://github.com/django/django/blob/2.2.1/django/contrib/admin/filters.py#L196 and unless ordering is defined on the related model's ModelAdmin class it stays an empty tuple. IMHO it should fall back to the ordering defined in the related model's Meta.ordering field.
RelatedOnlyFieldListFilter doesn't order the related model at all, even if ordering is defined on the related model's ModelAdmin class.
That's because the call to field.get_choices ​https://github.com/django/django/blob/2.2.1/django/contrib/admin/filters.py#L422 omits the ordering kwarg entirely.

</pr_description>

Now I can see both issues clearly:

1. In `RelatedFieldListFilter.field_choices` (line 196-201): When `related_admin` is None, ordering defaults to `()`. When it exists but `get_ordering` returns empty, it should fall back to `Model._meta.ordering`.

2. In `RelatedOnlyFieldListFilter.field_choices` (line 420-422): No `ordering` kwarg is passed to `field.get_choices`.

Let me check what `field.get_choices` does with the `ordering` parameter:

Now I understand the full picture. The `get_choices` method uses `ordering` parameter directly in `order_by(*ordering)`. When `ordering` is an empty tuple `()`, it means no ordering is applied (the default queryset ordering from Meta is cleared by `order_by()` - actually no, `order_by()` with no args clears any ordering. But `order_by(*())` is equivalent to `order_by()` which clears ordering).

Wait, let me check: `order_by(*())` - this unpacks to `order_by()` which indeed clears all ordering. So when `ordering=()`, the queryset won't use any ordering at all (not even Meta.ordering).
 
So the fix needs to handle the case where `ordering` is empty by falling back to the model's default ordering. I should update both `RelatedFieldListFilter.field_choices` and `RelatedOnlyFieldListFilter.field_choices` to check if `ordering` is empty, and if so, use `field.remote_field.model._meta.ordering` instead. Let me trace through how `get_ordering` works to see what it returns in different scenarios.
